title: Episodic experiment brief — convo-prefix cache sampler
content:
Goal: quick, reproducible personal tracker for small episodic inference runs that exercise convo-prefix/KV caching behavior and per-turn economics. Intent is to capture turn-level latency, cache hit-rate, and marginal cost for common convo patterns (short chit-chat vs long-context multi-turn).

Hypothesis: Enabling prefix caching (LRU policy, max-entries=3) will reduce per-turn p95 latency by ~20% for mid-length sessions (avg seq 600 tokens), but savings diminish when turn diversity is high (low cache hit-rate). Cost savings >2x only for high hit-rate reuse.

Setup notes:
- Model: rw-large-v1 (float16), baseline and quantized int8 variant.
- Hardware: single A100-40GB host (dev box).
- Runtime config: batching disabled, cache enabled for prefix only (no KV sharing across users).
- Seed prompts: 4 patterns (chit-chat, Q&A, code-edit, multi-topic long history).
- Measuring: per-turn latency p50/p95 (ms), tokens_out, cache_hit_pct, estimated token-cost (USD) using hosted unit cost 0.000003 per token-out (personal estimate).

Table (rows are individual session samples):
run_id,date,pattern,turns,avg_seq,cache_hit_pct,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_out,cost_usd,notes
EPI-001,2024-11-02,chit-chat,8,120,72,85,130,640,0.00192,high reuse after few turns
EPI-002,2024-11-03,qna,5,450,18,240,410,2300,0.0069,low reuse, long prompt per turn
EPI-003,2024-11-05,code-edit,10,520,64,190,320,4100,0.0123,reused function signatures -> good hit-rate
EPI-004,2024-11-10,multi-topic,12,760,9,410,780,9200,0.0276,bad reuse, cache thrash
EPI-005,2024-11-20,chit-chat,6,95,81,72,110,480,0.00144,very high reuse, steady p95
EPI-006,2024-12-01,qna,7,610,27,280,460,3500,0.0105,mixed reuse, quantized variant slightly faster p95

Quick observations:
- Clear correlation between cache_hit_pct and p95: sessions >60% hit see p95 < 200ms.
- Long context sessions (avg_seq >700) suffer high p95 regardless of hit-rate, likely due to attention kernel cost.
- Quantized int8 gives small p50 wins (~10-15%) but p95 improvements are workload-dependent.
- Estimated marginal token cost is dominated by total output tokens; caching only affects latency, not tokens_out (except when it enables shorter prompts).

Small action list (personal):
- A1: Re-run EPI-006 with max-entries=5 and measure hit-rate delta (target date: 2024-12-20).
- A2: Capture kernel-level CPU/GPU time for EPI-003 to identify attention hotspots.
- A3: Try lightweight prefix summarization (trim historical turns) for multi-topic pattern to improve reuse.
- A4: Add a column next run: prompt_tokens_in to approximate cache efficiency better.

Open questions / hypotheses to test later:
- Does adaptive prefix trimming (remove earliest low-similarity turns) improve effective hit-rate without hurting quality?
- How much does batching interact with prefix cache policies at small scale? (disabled here)
- For customers: what threshold of cache_hit_pct makes Dedicated worth it vs hosted? (back-of-envelope: >40% hits and avg_seq>400)

Scratch notes / raw commands used:
- run script: ./dev/run_sample_sessions.sh --pattern code-edit --seed 42 --cache-entries 3 --model rw-large-v1
- extract metrics: python tools/collect_turn_metrics.py --out epi-003-metrics.csv

Personal rating (quick):
- Repro complexity: low
- Value (directional): medium (helps prioritize cache policies in routing)

Next edits: convert to a tiny Confluence draft if A1 shows >10% p95 gains.

(End of sheet — informal, meant to be a living note. Will prune and formalize if patterns repeat.)
